items.title: Function app: sub-scoped hardcoded 'JIT Requester' check
items.description: Hardcode role name 'JIT Requester' in the app; remove JIT_REQUESTER_ROLE_NAME env usage. Change Test-CallerHasJitRequesterRole (JITHelpers.psm1:~315) to derive the subscription from the request body target subscriptionId instead of the site resource ID, resolve the role by name within the TARGET subscription, and check the caller's assignment at target-sub scope. Ensure the 'JIT Requester' role definition exists in each target subscription (Deploy.ps1/Grant-JITPermissions.ps1 create it per target sub). Keep 'JIT-AzAccess Manager' MI role untouched. Existing add-IP-to-whitelist + schedule-removal flow unchanged.

comments.author: developer
comments.text: Implemented. Two read endpoints had no request-body target sub, so a judgment call was made: Revoke-JITAccess checks against the rule's own subscription (row.SubscriptionId); Get-JITRules checks against the app's derived HOST subscription (it only returns the caller's own rules). Consequence: a user needs 'JIT Requester' in the host subscription to LIST rules, and in each target subscription to request/revoke there. Deploy Step 4 keeps the host sub in the role's assignableScopes so it isn't orphaned. NEEDS ARCHITECT/USER CONFIRMATION - listing one's own rules requiring a host-sub role may be undesirable.

comments.author: claude
comments.text: DECISION (user, 2026-07-16): Get-JITRules should have NO role check - any authenticated caller lists only their own rules. Follow-up change: remove the Test-CallerHasJitRequesterRole gate from Get-JITRules/run.ps1 (keep JWT/caller-identity validation for filtering), and drop the host subscription from the role's assignableScopes (revert Deploy.ps1 Step 4 host-sub merge). Requester role now lives ONLY in target subscriptions. Revoke stays checked against the rule's own subscription.

items.title: Fix stale mocks in Remove-ExpiredRules.Tests.ps1 (19 failing tests)
items.description: CORRECTED ROOT CAUSE (verified 2026-07-21): the 19 failing Remove-ExpiredRules.Tests.ps1 tests are NOT a Pester 3.4/PS7 incompatibility. Plain Pester 3.4 Mock/Assert-MockCalled works fine under PS7 (the 6 new postgres tests pass). The real cause: the stale BeforeEach mocks commands that no longer exist in the code (Get-JITCloudTable, Get-AzTableRow, Remove-AzTableRow) - Pester 3 cannot mock a nonexistent command, so every test in those Describes fails at setup with 'Could not find Command Get-JITCloudTable'. FIX: repoint those mocks to the current JITHelpers functions Get-JITTableName/Get-JITTableRows/Remove-JITTableRow (as the new postgres Describe already does) - NOT a Pester upgrade. SEPARATE/UNVERIFIED: the 2 JITHelpers.Tests.ps1 'Should Throw' failures were not re-diagnosed and may be a distinct issue. No CI runs these tests (publish-plugin.yml only builds the C# plugin).

comments.author: developer
comments.text: Additional finding (2026-07-21): Remove-ExpiredRules.Tests.ps1 mocks are also STALE vs implementation - they mock Get-AzTableRow/Remove-AzTableRow/Get-JITCloudTable, but current run.ps1 uses Get-JITTableRows/Remove-JITTableRow via Invoke-TableRest (not Az.Table). So the dispatch/retry assertions there never hit the real flow. The Pester-v5 upgrade should ALSO rewrite these mocks to the current JITHelpers functions.

items.title: PowerShell script: configure Azure PIM (permanent eligibility) for JIT-Requester across subscriptions
items.description: New src/scripts script. Params: -Subscriptions (list of sub IDs), -ActiveAssignment (Entra group display name -> permanent ACTIVE assignment), -EligibleAssignment (Entra group display name -> permanent ELIGIBLE assignment), -RoleName (default 'JIT-Requester'). Per subscription: resolve role def + group object IDs, relax the role management policy to ALLOW permanent eligibility (and permanent active), then create permanent (NoExpiration) eligible + active PIM assignments. PIM for Azure resources (ARM roleEligibilityScheduleRequests / roleAssignmentScheduleRequests). Idempotent, -WhatIf, per-sub summary. Requires PIM P2 licensing.

comments.author: developer
comments.text: Implemented as src/scripts/Set-JITPim.ps1 (Az.Accounts+Az.Resources; PIM for Azure resources). Verified cmdlet shapes vs MS Learn (azps-16.1.0). Policy relaxation: mutate EffectiveRule entries Expiration_Admin_Eligibility + Expiration_Admin_Assignment IsExpirationRequired=false. Permanent = -ExpirationType NoExpiration + -RequestType AdminAssign on New-AzRoleEligibilityScheduleRequest / New-AzRoleAssignmentScheduleRequest. Idempotent via Get-AzRoleEligibilitySchedule/Get-AzRoleAssignmentSchedule + conflict-catch; 3x15s retry for policy propagation. Syntax PARSE OK. LIVE EXECUTION NOT PERFORMED (no Az.Resources locally; needs P2 + Azure). First-run caveat: policy property assumed $policy.EffectiveRule - if the installed module differs the relaxation step errors clearly per-sub.

items.title: Enrich all JIT error messages with tenantId, subscription, and caller UPN
items.description: Function app: extend Write-JITAuditEvent (JITHelpers.psm1:508-546) with a tenantId field; thread $claims.tid; add tenantId/UPN/subscription to HTTP error bodies (centralize the 3 per-endpoint Write-JsonResponse copies); add the MISSING audit event on the Revoke role-denial (Revoke-JITAccess/run.ps1:104-107). Server already has UPN as $claims.upn. Plugin: add tenantId+subscription+resource to error toast/log Details (in scope at grant/revoke sites GrantFromTargetAsync ~1126, ConfirmRevokeAsync ~1205); put context in Details not the visible Message per INotifier guidance. OPEN DECISION: caller UPN is NOT available in the plugin (host exposes only TenantId+DisplayName; DisplayName is friendly name, not UPN). Options: server includes UPN in error bodies (covers 403 + server errors) and/or plugin fetches Graph GET /me per tenant (cached) for client-side-only errors. Note: expiry/timer path has no live token, so tenantId there needs persisting on the table row at grant time.

items.title: Plugin: retry-with-backoff on 403 role-denied grant (NOT token refresh)
items.description: User asked to 'refresh token and retry' on the 403 'caller does not hold JIT-Requester'. FINDING: token refresh is (a) IMPOSSIBLE via Contracts 1.3.0 - IPluginHttpClient.SendAsync has no forceRefresh, IPluginContext has no cache-invalidation, host overwrites auth header with a cached token; and (b) INEFFECTIVE anyway - server checks RBAC by the caller's stable oid via ARM at call time, not from token claims, so a fresh token changes nothing for a directly-assigned role; the real cause is RBAC propagation delay (~up to 5 min). EFFECTIVE FIX: bounded retry-with-backoff (2-3 attempts, short delay) on JitHttpException.StatusCode==403 inside GrantFromTargetAsync (wraps RequestAccessAsync ~JitAzAccessPlugin.cs:1096-1098); keep total under ~30-45s so the busy row doesn't hang. Branch on status code, not message text (plugin doesn't parse the message). GROUP-assignment edge case genuinely needs a fresh interactive login (host-owned) - only remedy is a re-sign-in guidance toast, or a Contracts enhancement request to host (IPluginContext.InvalidateToken -> existing CredentialFactory.Invalidate). OPEN DECISION: retry+re-sign-in hint vs retry-only vs retry+file host enhancement.

items.title: Reconcile AppName mismatch between Deploy.ps1 and Test-JITAccess.ps1
items.description: Deploy.ps1 uses $AppName='pgjitazaccess' while Test-JITAccess.ps1 defaults $AppName='jitazaccess'. These derive DIFFERENT resource names, so Test-JITAccess may target the wrong (non-existent) function app after a Deploy. Reconcile to a single source of truth.
